Otherwise it returns the current year minus one, which is 2025 today. I also added
all use these now. The "between X and
2100" error message is built from the same values.
Why current year minus one, not the current year:
the browser uses local time and the
server runs on UTC. For a few hours around New Year they disagree on the year, and
with the current year as the minimum the server would reject a year the browser just
accepted. One year of slack also covers someone who graduated in December and fills
the form in January without ticking the box. It still rejects a mistyped 2016. Saved
profiles aren't affected: a graduation date that has already passed reopens with the
box ticked, so older years stay valid.
This does change behaviour: current students can no longer enter 2020–2024. Before,
the test fixtures had fixed years like 2026, 2027 and 2030, which would start
failing once the minimum year passed them. I made them relative to the current year
and added a test for the minimum itself. All 13 tests pass, and
0 errors (the 19 warnings are all in other files).
